name: Former bullring (Palacio de Congresos) – Badajoz massacre memorial
story: After the city fell, Nationalist troops and Falangists rounded up militiamen, Popular Front supporters and people found with bruised shoulders from rifle recoil. Many were held in the bullring and shot there and elsewhere; bodies were burned and buried at the San Juan cemetery. Reports by Mário Neves, Jay Allen and other foreign journalists made 'Badajoz' known worldwide. The bullring was demolished in 2000 and the Palacio de Congresos 'Manuel Rojas' (2006) was built on the site within the San Roque bastion. After years of controversy a small permanent memorial display, 'Memorial Badajoz 1936', was installed in the lobby in 2021.
see: A modern congress hall on the site of the ring; in the lobby, information panels, a display case and audiovisual material on the massacre, plus a model of Blanca Muñoz's sculpture 'Eclíptica' that stands outside.
plan: The lobby is accessible when the building is open for events or office hours; check with the Palacio de Congresos (tel. 924 939 000). Outside, the sculpture can be seen any time.

boxes.text: Death toll strongly disputed: contemporary press reported 1,800–4,000 killed in the city; later historians (e.g. Francisco Espinosa) give several thousand victims in the city over the following months, while some revisionist authors argue for a few hundred. Whether mass shootings took place inside the bullring itself is also debated by the revisionist side.
